mission.beneficiary: Couples and small Discord groups who routinely remain in a voice channel at bedtime and want a safe, predictable way to disconnect later without waking up.
mission.consequential_choice: sequence: freeze broad feature expansion and prove the reliable scheduled-departure habit first; add VAD/STT and spoken interaction only if measured command friction is the main barrier to repeated use
falsifiers: Target users do not repeat the loop after an initial trial.
Users prefer Discord's existing controls or manual disconnection and do not consider scheduling meaningfully easier.
Reliable execution cannot reach the required level under real Discord connection and deployment conditions.
Users are uncomfortable granting the bot permission to disconnect themselves or others, even with explicit confirmation and cancellation.
Support and operating costs per repeated user outweigh the value of the narrow loop.
mission.interpretation: The project should not treat a general-purpose voice assistant as the product. The narrowest credible repeat loop is: schedule a voice-channel departure, receive an unambiguous confirmation, and have the bot execute it reliably. Voice input may later reduce friction, but only after the underlying action earns trust.
mission.mission: Make scheduled voice-channel departure a dependable nightly habit for Discord users who fall asleep together: create or join a departure schedule in seconds, confirm exactly who and when it affects, execute it reliably, and report the outcome.
mission.next_probe: Run a small instrumented pilot of the schedule-confirm-cancel-execute-result loop with bedtime voice-channel users, recording repeat nights per user, completion and cancellation rates, execution accuracy, mistaken-disconnection reports, confirmation-to-action latency, and operating cost; test typed commands first so voice-stack variability does not obscure demand.
non_goals: Building a broad conversational voice assistant.
Expanding music, newsletter, sports, travel, stock, or general AI features.
Using cloned-voice TTS as a prerequisite for the core loop.
Optimizing OpenRouter streaming or multilingual voice capabilities before repeat usage is demonstrated.
Supporting large-server orchestration before the bedtime use case is trusted.
mission.rationale: This mission directly matches the strongest user problem in the packet, is inherently repeatable, and uses the bot's existing scheduling identity. It also avoids making latency-sensitive STT, LLM, cloned-voice TTS, and local model operations prerequisites for delivering value. Reliability and consent matter more than conversational breadth when the bot can disconnect users.
mission.situation: GahyeonBot combines scheduling, music, newsletters, AI conversation, and an optional VAD-STT-LLM-TTS voice stack, but the frozen packet provides no observed usage, latency, trust, retention, or operating-cost evidence for any loop. Its clearest stated Discord-native pain is helping people leave a voice channel at a chosen time, especially before sleep.
mission.success_signal: Across a bounded pilot, the same users schedule departures on multiple nights, at least 95% of accepted schedules execute at the intended time and scope, cancellations remain easy, mistaken or surprising disconnections are rare, and users report that the feature replaces a recurring manual bedtime action.
